vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kwaishop-intelligent-diagnosis-skill-test
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is designed to generate business diagnosis reports by executing bash scripts that use 'curl' to interact with internal Kuaishou APIs (lego.corp.kuaishou.com). It explicitly instructs the agent to read sensitive credentials from local files (~/.openclaw/lang-bridge-key and ~/.openclaw/username) to authenticate these requests. While the behavior aligns with the stated purpose of an internal tool, the practice of constructing shell commands using unsanitized user input (e.g., the 'keyword' variable in Phase 3 of the diagnosis scripts) introduces a significant risk of shell injection. Additionally, the requirement for the agent to directly access local secret files is a high-risk capability that warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality (creating merchant/live/brand diagnostic reports) is plausible, but its runtime instructions require reading local secret files (~/.openclaw/lang-bridge-key and ~/.openclaw/username) and posting them to internal endpoints while claiming no required config — a mismatch that could expose credentials and deserves careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill's declared purpose (generate merchant/live/brand diagnostic reports) matches the actions described (call internal report/search endpoints). However the skill expects per-request access to local secret files for authentication rather than using declared credentials or a documented auth flow. The lack of any declared required config/env vars while the instructions depend on local files is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read local files (~/.openclaw/lang-bridge-key and ~/.openclaw/username) on every request and execute full curl POST commands that include those values to multiple internal endpoints. It also forbids use of other login skills and forbids splitting or modifying the provided bash commands. These instructions go beyond simple text-processing: they perform local file reads and network calls that transmit secrets, and they are not limited/declared in the skill metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files to write to disk, which minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires access to sensitive local configuration files (lang-bridge-key and username) but declares no required environment variables or config paths. Reading and transmitting those local secrets to external endpoints is disproportionate unless the user understands and consents to the exact keys and endpoint scope. The instructions do not document what the secret can access or its least-privilege boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not modify other skills or global agent settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed but is the platform default; by itself this is not flagged, though combining autonomous runs with secret access increases risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling this skill, confirm the following: (1) Verify the endpoints (lego.corp.kuaishou.com and baomai-smb.corp.kuaishou.com) and the skill owner are legitimate and that you trust them to receive your local secret. (2) Understand exactly what ~/.openclaw/lang-bridge-key and ~/.openclaw/username contain and whether those credentials are scoped/minimally privileged for report creation; if unsure, do not expose them. (3) Prefer an explicit, declared auth mechanism (environment variables or OAuth/SSO) instead of opaque per-request file reads; ask the author to document required config paths and the minimum permissions of the secret. (4) If you must run it, test in a least-privileged environment (with test/rotatable keys) and rotate any real secrets afterwards. (5) If the source is unknown or untrusted, do not install — request provenance, a homepage/repo, or a signed/official distribution before use.
